text:
jake: Hey @people-ops — quick question: my partner and I are starting a surrogacy route and there are a bunch of appointments and legal costs. Who do I talk to about (1) parental leave eligibility/timing for intended parents, (2) fertility/surrogacy expense reimbursement, and (3) paid time off for appointments + travel? thanks!

sophia (People Ops): Congrats — exciting ❤️. Short answers: parental leave is available to intended parents; fertility/surrogacy expenses are covered under the fertility benefits up to a cap; and there’s paid time off for medical appointments. I can DM details but here are the steps.

ana (People Ops): @jake — hi! high-level checklist: 1) designate primary vs secondary parent (this affects leave length) 2) submit leave request in HRIS with supporting docs (surrogacy agreement / placement letter) 3) open a benefits claim for reimbursement and upload receipts. I’ll drop links.

karen (Benefits): For reimbursements: our carrier covers up to $12,000 toward IVF/surrogacy-related medical expenses per calendar year; legal/travel reimbursements have a separate stipend up to $3,000. Submit claims via the benefits portal and email `benefits@redwood.com` to flag for expedited review. Keep originals of contracts/receipts.

jake: thanks! is there any pre-authorization needed for the medical stuff or just receipts? also any paid time off allowances for travel or multiple clinic visits?

karen (Benefits): For medical procedures, the carrier may require prior auth for some services — the clinic usually initiates that. For reimbursement we need: invoice, proof of service, and proof of payment. For travel/legal stipend, upload travel receipts + a brief note linking them to the surrogacy process.

ana (People Ops): Time-off: Redwood provides up to 10 paid days per calendar year for fertility- or surrogacy-related medical appointments (you don’t need to use vacation). Those are separate from parental leave. If you need more time (e.g., travel for placement), use parental leave or discuss unpaid leave / schedule adjustments with your manager.

luca (Manager): @jake — happy to be flexible. If you have estimated dates, ping me and I’ll coordinate coverage. We can also split handoff tasks as needed.

jake: awesome, appreciate it. one more: how does short-term disability (STD) / FMLA interplay for intended parents? do we file both?

ana (People Ops): Good Q. If you’re the primary parent and medically absent for placement-related procedures, you may be eligible for STD — file the STD claim and we’ll also help with FMLA paperwork if you qualify (FMLA eligibility = 12 months + 1,250 hours, depending on location). For non-medical placement days, STD won’t apply; use parental leave. We’ll DM the exact form links.

karen (Benefits): To summarize the claims flow: 1) open claim with carrier for medical expenses / STD 2) upload docs to benefits portal 3) cc `benefits@redwood.com` for company stipend reimbursement 4) People Ops will verify and update leave status in HRIS.

benefits-bot: Automated note — fertility & surrogacy benefits overview: https://intranet.redwood/benefits/fertility (policy summary + form links). Use code `SURROGACY2026` when submitting for internal routing.

jake: perfect. i'll gather docs and start the portal. who should i tag if i need help filling the STD or FMLA forms?

ana (People Ops): Tag me (ana) or DM `people-ops` channel. I can walk you through the HRIS form submission and which documents to attach. Also happy to coordinate confidentially.

karen (Benefits): If you hit any snags with carrier pre-auths, loop me in and I’ll escalate to the benefits rep.

jake: thanks all — will follow up once I have the surrogacy agreement and travel estimates. really appreciate the quick help :pray:
